1491.subject: Physics
1491.text: Time period of pendulum, on a satellite orbiting the earth, is
1491.sol:
On an artificial satellite orbiting the earth the acceleration is given by $\frac{G M}{R^2}$ towards the centre of the earth. Now for a body of mass $m$ on the satellite the graviational force due to earth is $\frac{G M m}{R^2}$ towards the centre of the earth. Let the reaction force on the surface of the satellite be $N$, then
$\frac{G M m}{R^2}-N=m\left(\frac{G M}{R^2}\right)$
$\Rightarrow \quad N=0$
That is on the satellite there is a state of weightlessness or $g=0$
$\therefore \quad$ The time period of the simple pendulum,
$T=2 \pi \sqrt{\frac{l}{g}}=\infty$

3641.subject: Chemistry
3641.text: Which of the following statements is correct for the cell $\mathrm{Zn}\left|\mathrm{Zn}^{+2}$\| $\mathrm{Cu}^{+2}$\right| $\mathrm{Cu}$ ?
3641.sol:
In the Daniell cell, copper and zinc electrodes are immersed in a solution of copper(II) sulphate and zinc sulphate, respectively.
At the anode (negative electrode), zinc is oxidised per the following half reaction.
\($\mathrm{Zn}($s) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}($a q)+2 e^{-}\)
At the cathode (positive electrode), copper is reduced per the following reaction.
\($\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}($a q)+2 e^{-} \longrightarrow $\mathrm{Cu}($s)\)
Overall cell reaction is
\($\mathrm{Zn}($s)+$\mathrm{Cu}^{2+}($a q) \longrightarrow $\mathrm{Zn}^{2+}($a q)+$\mathrm{Cu}($s)\)
These processes result in the accumulation of solid copper at the cathode and the corrosion of the zinc electrode into the solution as zinc cations. Hence, the correct option is (d).

5196.text:
Which of the following form an ideal sơlution?
I. Chloroethane and bromoethane
II. Benzene and toluene
III. $n$-hexane and $n$-heptane
IV. Phenol and aniline
5196.sol:
Ideal solutions are the solutions which obey Raoult's law at all temperatures and pressures. The $interactions of solute-solute, solvent-solvent and solute-solvent in these solutions are almost similar. No association/dissociation occurs in these solutions.
Mixture of phenol and aniline shows negative deviation from ideal behaviour and forms an azeotropic mixture. The phenol-aniline interactions are stronger than phenol-phenol or aniline-aniline interactions.
\begin{aligned} & \Delta V_{\text{mixing }} < 0 \\ & \Delta H_{\text{mixing }} > 0\end{aligned}$
Hence, it does not form an ideal solution.
Rest options (I), (II) and (III) form ideal solution.

\end{aligned} Now we will neglect term$ with  x^2$ and greater powers. i.e. $x^2=x^3=x^4=\ldots=x^n \approx 0$. \begin{aligned}& \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{3}[1-3 x+0+\ldots]\left[1+\frac{1}{6} x-0+\ldots\right] \\

& \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{3}\left(1-\frac{14}{6} x\right)=\frac{1}{3}\left(1-\frac{7}{3} x\right) \Rightarrow y=\frac{1}{3}-\frac{7}{9} x
\end{aligned}
$

9447.text:
If $f_n(x)=\log \log \log \ldots \log x \quad(\log$ is repeated $n$-times), then
$\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x$ is equal to
9447.sol:
$f_n(x)=\log \cdot \log \cdot \log \ldots \cdot \log x$ (upto $n$ times)
$f_1(x)=\log xf_2(x)=\log \log xf_3(x)=\log \log \log xf_{n-1}(x)=\log \log \log \ldots \ldots \log x$
(up to $(n-1)$ times)
Now, $\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x=\int \frac{d x}{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right]}=\int \frac{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] d t}{\left[x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] \cdot t}=\int \frac{d t}{t}=\log t+c\left[\begin{array}{l}\text{ Put, } f_n(x)=t \\ \frac{d t}{d x}=\frac{1}{\left[f_{n-1}(x) f_{n-2}(x) \ldots f_1(x) \cdot x\right]} \\ d x=\left[x f_1(x) \cdot f_2(x) \ldots f_{n-1}(x)\right] d t\end{array}\right]=\log f_n(x)+c=f_{n+1}(x)+c$
Hence,
$\int\left(x f_1(x) f_2(x) \ldots f_n(x)\right)^{-1} d x=f_{n+1}(x)+c$

$\frac{3 x^2+x+1}{(x-1)^4}=\frac{a}{(x-1)}+\frac{b}{(x-1)^2}+\frac{c}{(x-1)^3}+\frac{d}{(x-1)^4}3 x^2+x+1=a(x-1)^3+b(x-1)^2+c(x-1)+d3 x^2+x+1=a\left(x^3-1+3 x-3 x^2\right)+b\left(x^2+1-2 x\right)+c(x-1)+d3 x^2+x+1=a x^3+(-3 a+b) x^2+(3 a-2 b+c) x+(-a+b-c+d)$
On comparing the coefficient of like powers of $x$ on both sides.
$a=0,-3 a+b=3,3 a-2 b+c=2\Rightarrow \quad b=3 \Rightarrow 0-6+c=1\Rightarrow \quad c=7$
and $\quad-a+b-c+d=1\Rightarrow \quad 0+3-7+d=1\Rightarrow \quad d=5$
Hence, $\quad\left[\begin{array}{ll}a & b \\ c & d\end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ll}0 & 3 \\ 7 & 5\end{array}\right]$

11710.subject: Mathematics
11710.text: Let an angle of a triangle is $60 °$. If the variance of the angles of the triangle is $4614 °$, then the other two angles are
11710.sol:
Let three angles of triangle be& $x, y & z$.

As sum of three angles of triangle$= 180 °$.

$⇒ x + y + z = 180 °$

$⇒ 60 ° + y + z = 180 °$ (Given one angle is& ${60}^{∘}$)

$⇒ y + z = 120 ° \ldots \left(1\right)$

Now, it is given that variance of the angles of triangle is equal to $4614 °$.

$∴ \dfrac{x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2}}{3} =4614 °$

$⇒ \dfrac{\left({60}^{∘}\right)2 + y^{2} + z^{2}}{3} =4614 °$

$⇒ y^{2} + z^{2} = 10242 °$

$⇒ \left(y + z\right)2 - 2yz = 10242 °$

$⇒ 14400 ° - 2yz = 10242 °$ (Using& $\left(1\right)$)

$⇒ yz = 2079 ° \ldots \left(2\right)$

Now, $\left(y + z\right)2 = \left(y - z\right)2 + 4yz$

$⇒ \left(120\right) ° = \left($ y - z\right)2 + 4 \times2079 °$ (Using& \left(1\right) & \left(2\right)$)

$⇒ \left($ y - z\right)2 = 14400 ° - 8316 ° = 6084 °$

$⇒ y - z = 78 ° \ldots $\left(3\right)$

Solving equations $\left(1\right) & \left(3\right)$, we get,

$y = 99 ° & z = 21 °$

Thus, other two angles are $99 ° & 21 °$.

13476.text:
Let $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}=a_1 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a_2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a_3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Assertion (A) : The identity
$|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|^2=2|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}|^2$ holds for
$\vec{a}$.
Reason (R) : $\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}=a_3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-a_2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$,
$\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}=a_1 \hat{\mathbf{k}}-a_3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}, \overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}=a_2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-a_1 \hat{\mathbf{j}}$
Which of the following is correct?
options: Both $(\mathrm{A})$ and $(\mathrm{R})$ are true and $(\mathrm{R})$ is the correct reason for (A)
Both $(A)$ and $(R)$ are true but $(R)$ is not the correct reason for (A)
13476.sol:
Given,
$\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}=a_1 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a_2 \hat{\mathbf{j}}+a_3 \hat{\mathbf{k}}$
Now, $|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}|^2=(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}) \cdot(\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}})\begin{aligned} & =\left(a_3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-a_2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right) \cdot\left(a_3 \hat{\mathbf{j}}-a_2 \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right) \\ & =a_3^2+a_2^2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}|^2 & =\left(a_1 \hat{\mathbf{k}}-a_3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}\right) \cdot\left(a_1 \hat{\mathbf{k}}-a_3 \hat{\mathbf{i}}\right) \\ & =a_1^2+a_3^2\end{aligned}\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|^2 & =\left(a_1 \hat{\mathbf{i}}+a_1 \hat{\mathbf{j}}\right) \cdot\left(a_2 \hat{\mathbf{i}}-a_1 \hat{\mathbf{j}}\right) \\ & =a_2{ }^2+a_1{ }^2\end{aligned}$
Now,
$\begin{aligned}|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{i}}|^2 & +|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{j}}|^2+|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}} \times \hat{\mathbf{k}}|^2 \\ & =2\left(a_1^2+a_2^2+a_3^2\right) \\ & =2|\overrightarrow{\mathbf{a}}|^2\end{aligned}$
Hence, both $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{R}$ are true and $\mathrm{R}$ is correct reason for $\mathrm{A}$.

\phi$& =B A \\
& =\mu_0 N I_0 \sin $\omega$t $\times \frac{\pi^2 R^2}{4}$\\

\end{aligned}$Induced emf in the square coil, $e=\frac{d \phi}{d t}$

\end{aligned}

Equation of magnetic field of an electromagnetic wave is given by
$B=B_0 \sin (\omega t-k x) \hat{k}=B_0 \sin \left(2 \pi f t-\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda} \cdot x\right) \hat{k} \quad\left[\because \omega=2 \pi f\right.$ and $\left.k=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\right]=B_0 \sin \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}[f \lambda t-x] \hat{k}B=B_0 \sin \frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}[c t-x] \hat{k}$  ...(i)
Also direction of $\mathbf{B}$ vector is perpendicular to $\mathbf{E}$ and also to direction of propagation
And $B_0=\frac{E_0}{c}$
Here, $E_0=60 \mathrm{Vm}^{-1}\therefore \quad B_0=\frac{60^{}}{3 \times 10^8}=2 \times 10^{-7}$
Also $k=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}$
Here $k=200 \pi=\frac{2 \pi}{\lambda}\Rightarrow \quad \lambda=\frac{1}{100} \mathrm{~m}=\frac{100}{100} \mathrm{~cm}=10 \mathrm{~mm}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~m}$
Putting the values is eq. (i), we get
$B=2 \times 10^{-7} \sin \left[\frac{2 \pi}{10^{-2}}(c t-x)\right] \hat{k}=2 \times 10^{-7} \sin 200 \pi(t-x) \hat{k}$

19551.text: Identify $\mathrm{X}, \mathrm{Y}$ and Z formed in the reaction:
19551.sol:
The starting material is 4-formylcyclohexanone.

Reaction with $\text{Zn/Hg}$ and $\text{conc. HCl}$ is the Clemmensen reduction, which reduces both the ketone and the aldehyde groups to methylene groups. Thus, Z is 1-methyl-4-methylcyclohexane, which is simply 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane.

Reaction with $\text{Cu}^{+2}/\text{OH}^{-}$ (Fehling's solution or similar oxidizing conditions) selectively oxidizes the aldehyde group to a carboxylic acid group, while the ketone remains unaffected. Subsequent acidification with $\text{H}_3\textO^{+}$ gives 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid as X.

Reaction of X with $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the ketone group to a secondary alcohol, while the carboxylic acid group remains unaffected. Thus, Y is 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid.

Comparing these structures with the given options, the first option (yNO2a) correctly identifies X as 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid, Y as 4-hydroxycyclohexanecarboxylic acid, and Z as 1,4-dimethylcyclohexane.

20328.text: Toluene when reacted with $\mathrm{Cl}_2$ gas at 385 K forms a product X which undergoes further reaction with Sodium ethoxide to yield product Y. The structure of Y is ____。
20328.sol:
Toluene (C_6H_5CH_3$) reacts with $Cl_2$ gas at 385 K (which is a high temperature, often associated with free radical substitution) to form benzyl chloride (C_6H_5CH_2Cl$).

The reaction is: $C_6H_5CH_3 + Cl_2 \xrightarrow{385 K}$ C_6H_5CH_2Cl + HCl$.

Benzyl chloride (C_6H_5CH_2Cl$) then reacts with sodium ethoxide (NaOCH_2CH_3$), which is a strong nucleophile, via an $S_N2$ mechanism to form benzyl ethyl ether (C_6H_5CH_2OCH_2CH_3$).

The reaction is: $C_6H_5CH_2Cl + NaOCH_2CH_3 \rightarrow C_6H_5CH_2OCH_2CH_3 + NaCl$.

The structure of the product Y is benzyl ethyl ether, which corresponds to the fourth structure provided in the options.

20523.subject: Chemistry
20523.text: Which one of the following is an example of step growth polymerisation?
20523.sol:
Step growth polymerization, also known as condensation polymerization, involves the reaction of bifunctional or polyfunctional monomers with the elimination of small molecules like water, alcohol, or ammonia. In this process, the polymer chain grows by the reaction of any two species present in the mixture.

Nylon 6,6 is formed by the condensation reaction between hexamethylenediamine (H_{2}N(CH_{2})_{6}NH_{2}$) and adipic acid (HOOC(CH_{2})_{4}COOH$). This reaction proceeds with the elimination of water molecules, which is a characteristic feature of step growth polymerization.

In contrast, Buna-S, Neoprene, and Teflon are formed via chain growth polymerization (addition polymerization), where the reaction proceeds through the addition of monomer units to an active center (free radical or ionic) without the elimination of small molecules.

Answer: Nylon 6,6

21012.subject: Mathematics
21012.text: $\text{ The area (in sq units) enclosed by the parabola } y^2=8 x \text{, its latus-rectum and the } x \text{-axis$ is }
21012.sol:
The equation of the parabola is $y^2 = 8x$. Comparing this with $y^2 = 4ax$, we get $4a = 8$, which implies $a = 2$.

The latus-rectum of the parabola is the line $x = a = 2$.

The area enclosed by the parabola $y^2 = 8x$, the latus-rectum $x = 2$, and the $x$-axis is given by the integral of $y$ with respect to $x$ from $x = 0$ to $x = 2$.

Since $y^2 = 8x$, we have $y = \sqrt{8x} = 2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{x}$.

Area = $\int_{0}^{2} 2\sqrt{2}\sqrt{x} dx = 2\sqrt{2} \int_{0}^{2} x^{1/2} dx$.

Evaluating the integral: $2\sqrt{2} \left[ \dfrac{x^{3/2}}{3/2} \right]_{0}^{2} = 2\sqrt{2} \times \dfrac{2}{3} \times [x^{3/2}]_{0}^{2}$.

Area = $\dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} \times (2)^{3/2} = \dfrac{4\sqrt{2}}{3} \times 2\sqrt{2} = \dfrac{4 \times 2 \times 2}{3} = \dfrac{16}{3}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{16}{3}$

21987.subject: Mathematics
21987.text: A geometric progression consists of an even number of terms. If the sum of all the terms is five times the sum of the terms occupying the odd places, then the common ratio of the geometric progression is
21987.sol:
Let the geometric progression have $2n$ terms, given by $a, ar, ar^2, ar^3, \dots, ar^{2n-1}$.

The sum of all terms $S$ is given by $S = \dfrac{a(r^{2n} - 1)}{r - 1}$.

The terms occupying the odd places are $a, ar^2, ar^4, \dots, ar^{2n-2}$. This is a geometric progression with first term $a$, common ratio $r^2$, and $n$ terms.

The sum of terms in odd places $S_{odd}$ is given by $S_{odd} = \dfrac{a((r^2)^n - 1)}{r^2 - 1} = \dfrac{a(r^{2n} - 1)}{r^2 - 1}$.

According to the problem, $S = 5 S_{odd}$. Substituting the expressions:

$\dfrac{a(r^{2n} - 1)}{r - 1} = 5 \times \dfrac{a(r^{2n} - 1)}{r^2 - 1}$.

Since $r^{2n} - 1 \neq 0$ and $a \neq 0$, we can divide both sides by $a(r^{2n} - 1)$:

$\dfrac{1}{r - 1} = \dfrac{5}{r^2 - 1}$.

Since $r^2 - 1 = (r - 1)(r + 1)$, we have:

$\dfrac{1}{r - 1} = \dfrac{5}{(r - 1)(r + 1)}$.

Multiplying both sides by $(r - 1)$, we get $1 = \dfrac{5}{r + 1}$.

Therefore, $r + 1 = 5$, which implies $r = 4$.

Answer: $r=4$

From Einstein's photoelectric equation: $eV_s = h u - \Phi \Rightarrow V_s = \dfrac{h}{e} u - \dfrac{\Phi}{e}$

(4) Na has a lower threshold frequency \Rightarrow Na is more photosensitive than Al. So (4) is incorrect.

Correct option: (2)

23079.subject: Physics
23079.text:
Which of the following statements is CORRECT:
A. Paramagnetic property is an intrinsic property of the material that arises due to the presence of completely filled electron shells and does NOT depend on temperature.
B. Diamagnetic materials move from a region of weak magnetic field to strong magnetic field
C. Diamagnetic materials have negative magnetic susceptibility which means that they oppose the applied magnetic field
D. Paramagnetic materials have negative magnetic susceptibility which means that they oppose the applied magnetic field
23079.sol:
Paramagnetic materials possess unpaired electrons, which leads to their magnetic properties. This property is temperature-dependent, as described by Curie's Law, where susceptibility $\chi \propto \dfrac{1}{T}$. Thus, statement A is incorrect.

Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by magnetic fields. Consequently, they move from a region of strong magnetic field to a region of weak magnetic field. Thus, statement B is incorrect.

Diamagnetic materials exhibit negative magnetic susceptibility ($\chi < 0$). This indicates that the induced magnetic moment is in the direction opposite to the applied magnetic field, causing the material to be weakly repelled. Thus, statement C is correct.

Paramagnetic materials have positive magnetic susceptibility ($\chi > 0$), which means they are weakly attracted to an applied magnetic field. Thus, statement D is incorrect.

Answer: C

23441.subject: Physics
23441.text: A body of mass $5 \mathrm{ kg}$ at rest is rotated for $25 \mathrm{ s}$ with a constant moment of force $10 \mathrm{ Nm}$. Find the work done if the moment of inertia of the body is $5 \mathrm{ kg} \mathrm{ m}^2$.
23441.sol:
Given the moment of force (torque) $\tau = 10 \text{ Nm}$, moment of inertia $I = 5 \text{ kg m}^2$, and time $t = 25 \text{ s}$.

The angular acceleration $\alpha$ is given by $\tau = I \alpha$.

$\alpha = \dfrac{\tau}{I} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2 \text{ rad/s}^2$.

Since the body starts from rest, the initial angular velocity $\omega_0 = 0$. The angular velocity after time $t$ is $\omega = \omega_0 + \alpha t = 0 + 2 \times 25 = 50 \text{ rad/s}$.

The work done is equal to the change in rotational kinetic energy $W = \Delta K = \dfrac{1}{2} I \omega^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} I \omega_0^2$.

$W = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times (50)^2 - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times 2500 = 5 \times 1250 = 6250 \text{ J}$.

Answer: 6250 J

23644.subject: Physics
23644.text:
The interference pattern is obtained with two coherent light sources of intensity ratio $9: 1$.
The ratio of $\dfrac{I_{\text{MAX }}+I_{\text{MIN }}}{I_{\text{MAX }}-I_{\text{MIN }}}$ is $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$. The values of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are:
23644.sol:
Let the intensities of the two coherent sources be $I_1$ and $I_2$. Given the ratio $I_1 : I_2 = 9 : 1$, we can write $I_1 = 9k$ and $I_2 = k$ for some constant $k$.

The amplitudes $a_1$ and $a_2$ are proportional to the square root of the intensities, so $a_1 = \sqrt{9k} = 3\sqrt{k}$ and $a_2 = \sqrt{k}$.

The maximum intensity $I_{\text{MAX}}$ and minimum intensity $I_{\text{MIN}}$ in an interference pattern are given by $I_{\text{MAX}} = (\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2})^2$ and $I_{\text{MIN}} = (\sqrt{I_1} - \sqrt{I_2})^2$.

Substituting the values, $I_{\text{MAX}} = (3\sqrt{k} + \sqrt{k})^2 = (4\sqrt{k})^2 = 16k$ and $I_{\text{MIN}} = (3\sqrt{k} - \sqrt{k})^2 = (2\sqrt{k})^2 = 4k$.

The required ratio is $\dfrac{I_{\text{MAX}} + I_{\text{MIN}}}{I_{\text{MAX}} - I_{\text{MIN}}} = \dfrac{16k + 4k}{16k - 4k} = \dfrac{20k}{12k} = \dfrac{20}{12} = \dfrac{5}{3}$.

Comparing this with $\dfrac{\alpha}{\beta}$, we get $\alpha = 5$ and $\beta = 3$.

Answer: 5 and 3

24553.subject: Chemistry
24553.text: The correct order of ONO bond angle in the given species is
24553.sol:
For $\text{NO}_2^+$, the central nitrogen atom is $sp$ hybridized with no lone pairs, resulting in a linear geometry and a bond angle of $180^\circ$.

For $\text{NO}_2$, the central nitrogen atom is $sp^2$ hybridized with one unpaired electron. The repulsion from a single electron is less than that from a bond pair, so the bond angle opens up to be greater than $120^\circ$ (approximately $134^\circ$).

For $\text{NO}_3^-$, the central nitrogen atom is $sp^2$ hybridized with no lone pairs, resulting in a trigonal planar geometry and a bond angle of exactly $120^\circ$.

For $\text{NO}_2^-$, the central nitrogen atom is $sp^2$ hybridized with one lone pair. The lone pair-bond pair repulsion is greater than bond pair-bond pair repulsion, compressing the bond angle to less than $120^\circ$ (approximately $115^\circ$).

Therefore, the correct order of O-N-O bond angles is $\text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^- < \text{NO}_2 < \text{NO}_2^+$.

Answer: $\text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^- < \text{NO}_2 < \text{NO}_2^+$

In a circuit, a metal filament lamp is connected in series with a capacitor of capacitance $\mathrm{C} \mu F$ across a $200 \mathrm{~V}, 50 \mathrm{~Hz}$ supply. Given,

$P = 500W$

${V}_{R} = 100V$

$f = 50Hz$

${V}_{rms} = 200V$

$P = \dfrac{{{V}_{R}}^{2}}{R} ⇒ R = \dfrac{{{V}_{R}}^{2}}{P} ⇒ R = \dfrac{{\left(100\right)}^{2}}{500}$

$∴ R = 20Ω$

Now current in the circuit,

$i = {i}_{rms} = \dfrac{voltageacrossresistor}{resistance}i = \dfrac{100}{20}i = 5A$

Phasor diagram of the given circuit for voltage,

Now,

${V}^{2} = {{V}_{C}}^{2} + {{V}_{R}}^{2} ⇒ {200}^{2} = {{V}_{C}}^{2} + {100}^{2} ⇒ {V}_{C} = 100\sqrt{3}V$

Now,

${V}_{C} = 100\sqrt{3}V = I{X}_{C} ⇒ {X}_{C} = \dfrac{100\sqrt{3}}{5} = 20\sqrt{3}Ω$

and

26426.text: A particle of mass $m$ is moving in the $xy$-plane such that its velocity at a point $( x, y )$ is given as $\overset{\to}{v} = \alpha\left(y\overset{∧}{x} + 2x\overset{∧}{y}\right)$ where $\alpha$ is a non-zero constant. What is the force $\overset{\to}{F}$ acting on the particle?
26426.sol:
As force is given by, $\overset{\to}{F} = m\dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt}$.

Given: $\overset{\to}{v} = \alpha\left(y\overset{∧}{x} + 2x\overset{∧}{y}\right)$, where velocity along x-axis is ${v}_{x} = \alphay$ and velocity along y-axis is ${v}_{y} = 2x\alpha$.

Therefore,

$\dfrac{d\overset{\to}{v}}{dt} = \alpha\left(\dfrac{dy}{dt}\overset{∧}{x} + 2\dfrac{dx}{dt}\overset{∧}{y}\right)$

$= \alpha\left({v}_{y}\overset{∧}{x} + 2{v}_{x}\overset{∧}{y}\right)$

$= \alpha\left[2x\alpha\overset{∧}{x} + 2\alphay\overset{∧}{y}\right]$

$= 2{\alpha}^{2}\left[x\overset{∧}{x} + y\overset{∧}{y}\right]$

Therefore, required value of $\overset{\to}{F} = 2m{\alpha}^{2}\left[x\overset{∧}{x} + y\overset{∧}{y}\right]$.

28307.text: If 50 % of a reaction occurs in 100 second and 75 % of the reaction occurs in 200 second, the order of this reaction is:
28307.sol:
50% of a reaction occurs in 100 second and 75% of the reaction occurs in 200 second, the order of this reaction is 1.

Let the initial reactant concentration is 1 M.

In the first 100 seconds, reactant concentration is reduced to $50 % or1 \times \dfrac{50}{100} ​ = 0 . 5M .$

In the second 100 seconds (total 200 seconds from start), reactant concentration is reduced to $100 - 75 = 25 % or1 \times \dfrac{25}{100} ​ = 0 . 25M .$.

Thus, we observe that after each 100 second period, the reactant concentration is reduced to one half. Hence, 100 seconds is the half-life period and is independent of reactant concentration. This is characteristic of the first-order reaction.



First-order reaction as the half-life is constant.

28459.chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
28459.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
Electronic configuration of neutral atom (where $n=2$)		List-II
$1^{st}$ Ionization Energy (kJ mol$^{-1}$)
A. $ns^2$I. $2080$
B. $ns^2np^1$II. $899$
C. $ns^2np^3$III. $800$
D. $ns^2np^6$IV. $1402$
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
28459.sol:
Given $n=2$, the electronic configurations correspond to elements of the second period.

A. $ns^2 \Rightarrow 2s^2$ is Beryllium (Be).
B. $ns^2np^1 \Rightarrow 2s^2 2p^1$ is Boron (B).
C. $ns^2np^3 \Rightarrow 2s^2 2p^3$ is Nitrogen (N).
D. $ns^2np^6 \Rightarrow 2s^2 2p^6$ is Neon (Ne).

The first ionization energy generally increases across a period from left to right. However, Beryllium has a higher ionization energy than Boron due to the stable fully-filled $2s$ subshell. Nitrogen has a high ionization energy due to its stable half-filled $2p$ subshell. Neon, being a noble gas, has the highest ionization energy.

The order of first ionization energy is B $<$ Be $<$ N $<$ Ne.

Arranging the given values in increasing order: $800 < 899 < 1402 < 2080$ kJ mol$^{-1}$.

Thus, the matching is:
A. Be $\rightarrow 899$ (II)
B. B $\rightarrow 800$ (III)
C. N $\rightarrow 1402$ (IV)
D. Ne $\rightarrow 2080$ (I)

This corresponds to A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I

28669.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Hybridisation, shape and spin only magnetic moment of $\mathrm{K}_{3}\left[\mathrm{Co}\left(\mathrm{CO}_{3}\right)_{3}\right]$ is $\mathrm{sp}^{3} \mathrm{~d}^{2}$, octahedral and 4.9 BM respectively.
Statement II: Geometry, hybridisation and spin only magnetic moment values $(\mathrm{BM})$ of the ions $\left[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CN})_{4}\right]^{2-},\left[\mathrm{MnBr}_{4}\right]^{2-}$ and $\left[\mathrm{CoF}_{6}\right]^{3-}$ respectively are square planar, tetrahedral, octahedral; $\mathrm{dsp}^{2}, \mathrm{sp}^{3}, \mathrm{sp}^{3} \mathrm{~d}^{2}$ and $0,5.9,4.9$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
28669.sol:
In Statement I, for $K_3[Co(CO_3)_3]$, Cobalt is in $+3$ oxidation state ($Co^{3+}: 3d^6$). Carbonate ($CO_3^{2-}$) is a weak field ligand. Thus, no pairing occurs, resulting in 4 unpaired electrons. Hybridisation is $sp^3d^2$, shape is octahedral, and $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.9$ BM. Statement I is true.
In Statement II:
For $[Ni(CN)_4]^{2-}$, $Ni^{2+}$ is $3d^8$. $CN^-$ is a strong field ligand, causing pairing. Hybridisation is $dsp^2$, geometry is square planar, and $\mu = 0$ BM.
For $[MnBr_4]^{2-}$, $Mn^{2+}$ is $3d^5$. $Br^-$ is a weak field ligand. Hybridisation is $sp^3$, geometry is tetrahedral, and $\mu = \sqrt{5(5+2)} = \sqrt{35} \approx 5.9$ BM.
For $[CoF_6]^{3-}$, $Co^{3+}$ is $3d^6$. $F^-$ is a weak field ligand. Hybridisation is $sp^3d^2$, geometry is octahedral, and $\mu = \sqrt{4(4+2)} = \sqrt{24} \approx 4.9$ BM.
Statement II is true.
Both statements are true.

32536.subject: Chemistry
32536.text: At the transition temperature $T$, $A \rightleftharpoons B$ and $\Delta G^0 = 105 - 35\log T$ where $A$ and $B$ are two states of substance $X$. The transition temperature in $°$C when pressure is $1$ atm is _______. (Nearest integer)
32536.sol:
At the transition temperature and $1$ atm pressure, the two states $A$ and $B$ are in equilibrium.

For a phase transition of a pure substance at $1$ atm, both states are in their standard states, so the reaction quotient $Q = 1$.

Using the relation $\Delta G = \Delta G^0 + RT \ln Q$, we get $\Delta G = \Delta G^0$.

At equilibrium, $\Delta G = 0$, which implies $\Delta G^0 = 0$.

Given $\Delta G^0 = 105 - 35\log T$, we can equate it to zero:

$105 - 35\log T = 0$

$35\log T = 105$

$\log T = 3$

$T = 10^3 = 1000$ K

Converting the temperature to Celsius:

$T(^{\circ}\text{C}) = 1000 - 273 = 727^{\circ}\text{C}$

Answer: $727$

32926.text: If the curves $x = {y}^{4}$ and $xy = k$ cut at right angles, then ${\left(4k\right)}^{6}$ is equal to ___ .
32926.sol:
Given, $x = {y}^{4}$and $xy = k$

By solving equations, we get ${y}^{5} = k \ldots \left(1\right)$

Also $x = {y}^{4}$

$⇒ 1 = 4{y}^{3}\dfrac{dy}{dx} ⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{1}{4{y}^{3}}$

for $xy = k ⇒ x = \dfrac{k}{y}$

$⇒ 1 = - \dfrac{k}{{y}^{2}} \cdot \dfrac{dy}{dx}$

$⇒ \dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{- {y}^{2}}{k}$

$∵$ Curve cut orthogonally

$⇒ y = \dfrac{1}{4k}$

$∴$ from $\left(1\right){y}^{5} = k$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{{\left(4k\right)}^{5}} = k$

$⇒ 4 = {\left(4k\right)}^{6}$

\end{aligned} .$

34144.text: Let $[\cdot]$ be the greatest integer function. If $\alpha=\int_{0}^{64}\left(x^{1 / 3}-\left[x^{1 / 3}\right]\right) \mathrm{d} x$, then $\frac{1}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\alpha \pi}\left(\frac{\sin ^{2} \theta}{\sin ^{6} \theta+\cos ^{6} \theta}\right) \mathrm{d} \theta$ is equal to $\_\_\_\_$ .
34144.sol:
$\because \int_{0}^{64} x^{\frac{1}{3}} \, dx = \dfrac{3}{4} \left[ x^{\frac{4}{3}} \right]_{0}^{64} = 192$ &
$\int_{0}^{64} [x^{1/3}] \, dx = \int_{0}^{1} [x^{1/3}] \, dx + \int_{1}^{8} [x^{1/3}] \, dx + \int_{8}^{27} [x^{1/3}] \, dx + \int_{27}^{64} [x^{1/3}] \, dx = 156$
So $\alpha = 192 - 156 = 36$
Now $E = \dfrac{1}{\pi} \int_{0}^{36\pi} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$
$= \dfrac{36}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$
$\Rightarrow E = \dfrac{36 \cdot 2}{\pi} \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$
Let $J = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$ ....(1)
Applying King
$J = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$ .....(2)
Now $2J = \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{1}{\sin^6\theta + \cos^6\theta} \, d\theta$ (add (1) & (2))
$= \int_{0}^{\pi/2} \dfrac{\sec^6\theta}{\tan^6\theta + 1} \, d\theta$
$= \int_{0}^{\infty} \dfrac{(1 + \lambda^2)}{\lambda^4 - \lambda^2 + 1} \, d\lambda$
$= \int_{0}^{\infty} \dfrac{1 + \dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}}{\lambda^2 - 1 + \dfrac{1}{\lambda^2}} \, d\lambda$
$= \pi$
$\Rightarrow J = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
$\Rightarrow E = \dfrac{36 \cdot 2}{\pi} \times J = 36$

34249.text: The minimum value of the twice differentiable function $f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}, x \in R$, is
34249.sol:
Given,

$f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{x - t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}{∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{- t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ {e}^{- x}f\left(x\right) = {∫}_{0}^{x}{e}^{- t}{f}^{'}\left(t\right)dt - \left({x}^{2} - x + 1\right)$

Differentiate on both side w.r.t $x$ we get,

${e}^{- x}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) + \left(- f\left(x\right){e}^{- x}\right) = {e}^{- x}{f}^{'}\left(x\right) - 2x + 1$

$⇒ f\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2\right) + {e}^{x}\left(2x - 1\right)$

$⇒ {f}^{'}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x + 1\right) . . . . . . \left(1\right)$

Now finding critical point we get,

$2x + 1 = 0 ⇒ x = - \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now differentiating equation $\left(1\right)$ to check maxima and minima we get,

${f}^{"}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2\right) + \left(2x + 1\right){e}^{x}$

$⇒ {f}^{"}\left(x\right) = {e}^{x}\left(2x + 3\right)$

For $x = - \dfrac{1}{2}, {f}^{"}\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) > 0$, so it will give point of minima,

Now minimum value will be given by, $f\left(\dfrac{- 1}{2}\right) = {e}^{- \dfrac{1}{2}}\left(- 1 - 1\right) = - \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{e}}$

34442.text:
Let n be the number obtained on rolling a fair die. If the probability that the system
$x-\mathrm{n} y+z=6$
$x+(\mathrm{n}-2) y+(\mathrm{n}+1) z=8$
$(\mathrm{n}-1) y+z=1$ has a unique solution is $\frac{k}{6}$,
then the sum of $k$ and all possible values of $n$ is :
34442.sol:
The coefficient matrix has determinant $\det(A) = -(n-1)(n-2)$.
The system has a unique solution when $\det(A) eq 0$, which requires $n eq 1$ and $n eq 2$.
For a fair die, $n \in \{1,2,3,4,5,6\}$, so the unique solution occurs for $n \in \{3,4,5,6\}$.
The probability is $ rac{4}{6} = rac{2}{3}$, giving $k = 4$.
The sum of $k$ and all possible values of $n$ where unique solution exists is $4 + (3+4+5+6) = 22$.

34591.text:
Let $S$ be the set of all real values of $k for $which the system of linear equations

$\begin{aligned}
&x+y+z=2 \\
&2 x+y-z=3 \\
&3 x+2 y+k z=4
\end{aligned}$

has a unique solution. Then$S$ is
options:
an empty set

equal to $\mathrm{R}-\{0\}$

equal to $\{0\}$

equal to $\mathrm{R}$
34591.sol:
The system of linear equations is:
$$
\begin{aligned}
&x+y+z=2 \\
&2 x+y-z=3 \\
&3 x+2 y+k z=4
\end{aligned}
$$
As, system has unique solution.
$$
\begin{aligned}
&\text{ So, }\left|$\begin{array}{ccc}
1 & 1 & 1 \\
2 & 1 & -1 \\
3 & 2 & k
\end{array}$\right| \neq 0 \\
&\Rightarrow k+2-(2 k+3)+1 \neq 0 \\
&\Rightarrow k \neq 0
\end{aligned}
$$
Hence, $k \in R-\{0\} \equiv S$

35228.text: The number of one-one functions $f: \left\{a, b, c, d\right\} \to \left\{0, 1, 2, \ldots , 10\right\}$ such that $2f\left(a\right) - f\left(b\right) + 3f\left(c\right) + f\left(d\right) = 0$ is _____
35228.sol:
Given $2f\left(a\right) + 3f\left(c\right) = f\left(b\right) - f\left(d\right)$

Using fundamental principle of counting,

when $f\left(c\right) = 0, f\left(a\right) = 1\text{then}f\left(b\right) - f\left(d\right) = 2$ has $7$ choices,

Similarly when $f\left(c\right) = 0, f\left(a\right) = 2\text{then}f\left(b\right) - f\left(d\right)$ has $5$ choices.

Counting like this we get the total number of one-one function as $31$

Now $L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{{x}^{2} - ax + b}{x - 1}$ $\left(\dfrac{0}{0}\right)$ form

By using L'Hospital Rule,

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{2x - a}{1}$

$⇒ L = \lim_{x \to 1}\dfrac{2x - a}{1} = 5$

$⇒ 2 - a = 5 ⇒ a = - 3$

From the equation $\left(1\right),$ we get

$⇒ b = a - 1 = - 4$

$⇒ a + b = - 7 .$

Perpendicular distance of point $P$ from the plane is

Perpendicular distance of point $Q$ from the plane is

$= \left|\dfrac{- 2 - 1 + 3 - 1}{\sqrt{{1}^{2} + {1}^{2} + {1}^{2}}}\right| = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{PQ}$ is parallel to given plane. So, distance between $P and Q =$ distance between their foot of perpendiculars.

$⇒ \overset{\to}{\left|PQ\right|} = \sqrt{{\left(1 - 2\right)}^{2} + {\left(2 + 1\right)}^{2} + - {\left(1 - 3\right)}^{2}}$

$= \sqrt{26}$

$\overset{\to}{\left|PQ\right|}2 = 26 = {d}^{2}$

38235.text: Equation of the line of the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x ⁡}{1} = \dfrac{y ⁡}{- 1} = \dfrac{z ⁡}{1}$ and $\dfrac{x ⁡ - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y ⁡ + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z ⁡}{1}$ is
38235.sol:
The equation of a line of the shortest distance between the given lines will be along the perpendicular to both the lines.

A line perpendicular to ${L}_{1}: \dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ and ${L}_{2}: \dfrac{x - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z}{1}$ is,

$\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & - 1 & 1 \\ 0 & - 2 & 1\end{cases}\right| = \overset{^}{i}\left(- 1 + 2\right)$ - \overset{^}{j}$\left(1 - 0\right)$ + \overset{^}{k}$\left(- 2 + 0\right)$

$= \overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

Let, $\dfrac{x}{1} = \dfrac{y}{- 1} = \dfrac{z}{1} =$\alpha$

$⇒ x = \alpha, y = - \alpha, z = \alpha$

Thus, a point on the line ${L}_{1}$ is $P ( \alpha, - \alpha, \alpha )$

Similarly, let \dfrac{x - 1}{0} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 2} = \dfrac{z}{1} =$\lambda$

$⇒ x = 1, y = - 2\lambda - 1, z = \lambda$

Thus, a point on the line ${L}_{2}$ is $Q ( 1, - 1 - 2\lambda, \lambda )$

Now, a vector joining the points $P $\text{$ and } Q$ is $( \alpha - 1 ) \overset{^}{i} + ( 2\lambda - \alpha + 1 ) \overset{^}{j} + ( \alpha - \lambda ) \overset{^}{k}$

Let, the vector joining the points $P $\text{$ and } Q$ is along perpendicular to the two lines.

Hence, $( \alpha - 1 ) \overset{^}{i} + ( 2\lambda - \alpha + 1 ) \overset{^}{j} + ( \alpha - \lambda ) \overset{^}{k}$ and $\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} - 2\overset{^}{k}$ are

proportional and hence on comparing, \dfrac{\alpha - 1}{1} = \dfrac{\alpha - 2\lambda - 1}{1} = \dfrac{\lambda - \alpha}{2}$

$⇒ \alpha - 1 = \alpha - 2\lambda - 1$

$⇒ \lambda = 0$

Hence, point $Q$ is $\left(1, - 1, 0\right)$

The equation of a line passing through a point $\left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}, {z}_{1}\right)$ and parallel to a vector $a\overset{^}{i} + b\overset{^}{j} + c\overset{^}{k}$ is $\dfrac{x - {x}_{1}}{a} = \dfrac{y - {y}_{1}}{b} = \dfrac{z - {z}_{1}}{c}$

So, the equation of required line is $\dfrac{x - 1}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{- 1} = \dfrac{z}{- 2} .

$

38397.text: The value of $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$ is equal to:
38397.sol:
Given, $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

Now by we know that $sin\left(\theta\right) = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$, so by using this we get $sin\dfrac{\pi}{22} = cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{22}\right) = cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11}$ and similarly $sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{3\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22} = \dfrac{2\pi}{11}, sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22} = cos\dfrac{\pi}{11}$

So, $2sin\dfrac{\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{3\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{5\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{7\pi}{22}sin\dfrac{9\pi}{22}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{3\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{1\pi}{11}$

$= 2cos\dfrac{1\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

{As $cos\dfrac{3\pi}{22} = - cos\left(\pi - \dfrac{3\pi}{11}\right) = - cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}$ and $cos\dfrac{5\pi}{11} = - cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$}

$= \dfrac{2sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}{2sin\dfrac{\pi}{11}}cos\dfrac{\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{2\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{4\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{8\pi}{11}cos\dfrac{16\pi}{11}$

39270.subject: Physics
39270.chapter: Center of Mass, Momentum and Collision
39270.text: Two blocks of masses $2$ kg and $1$ kg respectively, are tied to the ends of a string which passes over a light frictionless pulley as shown in the figure below. The masses are held at rest at the same horizontal level and then released. The distance traversed by the centre of mass in $2$ s is _______ m. (Take $g = 10$ m/s$^2$)
39270.sol:
The acceleration of the blocks in the Atwood machine is given by:

$a = \dfrac{m_1 - m_2}{m_1 + m_2} g$

Substituting the given values ($m_1 = 2$ kg, $m_2 = 1$ kg):

$a = \dfrac{2 - 1}{2 + 1} g = \dfrac{g}{3}$

Taking the downward direction as positive, the acceleration of the $2$ kg block is $a_1 = \dfrac{g}{3}$ and the acceleration of the $1$ kg block is $a_2 = -\dfrac{g}{3}$.

The acceleration of the centre of mass is:

$a_{cm} = \dfrac{m_1 a_1 + m_2 a_2}{m_1 + m_2}$

$a_{cm} = \dfrac{2 \left(\dfrac{g}{3}\right) + 1 \left(-\dfrac{g}{3}\right)}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{\dfrac{g}{3}}{3} = \dfrac{g}{9}$

Since the system is released from rest, the initial velocity of the centre of mass is zero.

The distance traversed by the centre of mass in $t = 2$ s is:

$S_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2} a_{cm} t^2$

$S_{cm} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left(\dfrac{10}{9}\right) (2)^2 = \dfrac{20}{9} \approx 2.22 \text{ m}$

Answer: $2.22$

39915.subject: Physics
39915.text:
An electron of mass $m$ is moving in an electric field $\vec{E} = -2E_0\hat{i}$ ($E_0 =$ constant $> 0$), with an initial velocity $\vec{V} = v_0\hat{i}$ ($v_0 =$ constant $> 0$). If $\lambda_0 = \dfrac{h}{4mv_0}$, its de Broglie wavelength at time $t$ is __________.
($e =$ charge of electron)
39915.sol:
The force experienced by the electron in the electric field is given by $\vec{F} = q\vec{E}$.

Since the charge of an electron is $-e$ and the electric field is $\vec{E} = -2E_0\hat{i}$, the force is:

$\vec{F} = (-e)(-2E_0\hat{i}) = 2eE_0\hat{i}$

The acceleration of the electron is:

$\vec{a} = \dfrac{\vec{F}}{m} = \dfrac{2eE_0}{m}\hat{i}$

Using the first equation of motion, the velocity of the electron at time $t$ is:

$\vec{v}(t) = \vec{V} + \vec{a}t = \left(v_0 + \dfrac{2eE_0}{m}t\right)\hat{i}$

The de Broglie wavelength of the electron at time $t$ is:

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m|\vec{v}(t)|} = \dfrac{h}{m\left(v_0 + \dfrac{2eE_0}{m}t\right)}$

We are given that $\lambda_0 = \dfrac{h}{4mv_0}$, which implies $h = 4mv_0\lambda_0$. Substituting this into the expression for $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{4mv_0\lambda_0}{m\left(v_0 + \dfrac{2eE_0}{m}t\right)}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $mv_0$, we get:

$\lambda = \dfrac{4\lambda_0}{1 + \dfrac{2E_0 e}{m}\dfrac{t}{v_0}}$

Answer: $\dfrac{4\lambda_0}{\left[1 + \dfrac{2E_0 e}{m}\dfrac{t}{v_0}\right]}$

43692.subject: Physics
43692.text: Two conductors have the same resistances at $0 ° C$ but their temperature coefficients of resistance are ${\alpha}_{1}$ and ${\alpha}_{2}$. The respective temperature coefficients for their series and parallel combinations are :
43692.sol:
Change in resistance due to temperature is given by, ${R}^{'} = R\left(1 + \alpha ∆ T\right)$

For Series Combination:

${R}_{eq} = {R}_{1} + {R}_{2}$

$⇒ 2R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right) + R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)$

$⇒ 2R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right) = 2R + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right)R ∆ T$

$⇒ {\alpha}_{eq} = \dfrac{{\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}}{2}$

For Parallel Combination:

$\dfrac{1}{{R}_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{{R}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{R}_{2}}$

$⇒ \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{R}{2}\left(1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right)} = \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)} + \dfrac{1}{R\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1}{1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T} + \dfrac{1}{1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T}$

$⇒ \dfrac{2}{1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T} = \dfrac{1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T + 1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T}{\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)}$

$⇒ 2\left[\left(1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T\right)\left(1 + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right)\right] = \left[2 + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T\right]\left[1 + {\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T\right]$

$⇒ 2\left[1 + {\alpha}_{1} ∆ T + {\alpha}_{2} ∆ T + {\alpha}_{1}{\alpha}_{2} ∆ T\right] = 2 + 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T + {\alpha}_{eq}\left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ {T}^{2}$

Neglecting small terms

$2 + 2\left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T = 2 + 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T + \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T$

$⇒ \left({\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}\right) ∆ T = 2{\alpha}_{eq} ∆ T$

$⇒ {\alpha}_{eq} = \dfrac{{\alpha}_{1} + {\alpha}_{2}}{2}$

43704.subject: Physics
43704.text: A body cools from $60 ° C$ to $40 ° C$ in $6$ minutes. If, temperature of surroundings is $10 ° C$. Then, after the next $6$ minutes, its temperature will be ______ $° C$.
43704.sol:
From Newton’s law of cooling

$\dfrac{d T}{d t} = k\left({T}_{avg} - {T}_{0}\right)$, here, ${T}_{0}$ is surrounding temperature.

For case $1$:

$\dfrac{60 - 40}{6} = k\left(\dfrac{60 + 40}{2} - 10\right)$

$\dfrac{20}{6} = k\left(50 - 10\right) . . . \left(1\right)$

For case $2$:

$\dfrac{40 - T}{6} = k\left(\dfrac{40 + T}{2} - 10\right) . . . \left(2\right)$

From equation $\left(1\right)$, we have $k = \dfrac{1}{12}$

Putting in equation $\left(2\right)$

$\dfrac{40 - T}{6} = \dfrac{1}{12}\left(\dfrac{40 + T}{2} - 10\right)$

$⇒ 10 + \dfrac{T}{2} = 80 - 2T ⇒ 2T + \dfrac{T}{2} = 70$

$⇒ T = \dfrac{140}{5} = 28 ° C$

46827.sol:

Acromegaly has many unusual signs, including hand and foot enlargement, joint pain, tighter skin, deepening of the voice, headaches, and vision issues.
Excessive growth of bones and enlargement of internal organs is caused by gigantism. Gigantism contributes to severe linear development, headaches, etc.

50432.text:
Moment of Inertia of a thin uniform rod rotating about the perpendicular axis passing through
its centre is \( I \). If the same rod is bent into a ring and its moment of inertia about its diameter is
\( I^{\prime} \) then the ratio \( $\frac{I}{I^{\prime}}$\) is
50432.sol:
Moment of inertia of a thin uniform rod is given as
\[ I=$\frac{M L^{2}}{12}$\]
Moment of inertia of a ring is given as
\[ I^{\prime}=$\frac{M R^{2}}{2}$\]
Therefore \( $\frac{I}{I}=\frac{\left(\frac{M L^{2}}{12}\right)}{\left(\frac{M R^{2}}{2}\right)}=\frac{L^{2}}{6 R^{2}}$\)
Now, \( L=2 \Pi R \)
Thus \( $\frac{I}{I}=\frac{(2 \Pi)^{2} R^{2}}{6 R^{2}}=\frac{4 \Pi^{2}}{6}=\frac{2 \Pi^{2}}{3}$\)

55800.subject: Chemistry
55800.text: Which of the following compounds has maximum covalent character?
55800.sol:
Fajan's rules determine covalent character based on cation size, anion size, and ion charge. Smaller cations and larger anions increase covalent character due to greater polarizing power and polarizability.

The Li$^+$ cation is smaller than Na$^+$ since lithium is in period 2 while sodium is in period 3. Compounds with Li$^+$ therefore exhibit greater covalent character.

Between chloride and iodide anions, I$^-$ is larger than Cl$^-$ as iodine is in period 5 while chlorine is in period 3. The larger iodide anion contributes to increased covalent character.

LiI combines the small Li$^+$ cation with the large I$^-$ anion, maximizing covalent character among the options.

56676.subject: Chemistry
56676.text: Which from following elements is NOT regarded as transition element?
56676.sol:
Transition elements are defined as those having an incompletely filled d-subshell in their ground state or common oxidation states.

Nickel (Ni, Z=28) has ground state configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^8 4s^2$, and $\mathrm{Ni}^{2+}$ configuration $[\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^8$, showing incomplete d-subshell.

Iron (Fe, Z=26) has ground state $[\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^6 4s^2$, with $\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}$ at $[\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^6$ and $\mathrm{Fe}^{3+}$ at $[\mathrm{Ar}]\ 3d^5$, both incomplete.

Silver (Ag, Z=47) has ground state $[\mathrm{Kr}]\ 4d^{10} 5s^1$. While $\mathrm{Ag}^+$ is $[\mathrm{Kr}]\ 4d^{10}$ (complete), $\mathrm{Ag}^{2+}$ is $[\mathrm{Kr}]\ 4d^9$, exhibiting an incomplete d-subshell.

Mercury (Hg, Z=80) has ground state $[\mathrm{Xe}]\ 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^2$. Both $\mathrm{Hg}^{2+}$ ($[\mathrm{Xe}]\ 4f^{14} 5d^{10}$) and $\mathrm{Hg}^+$ ($[\mathrm{Xe}]\ 4f^{14} 5d^{10} 6s^1$) maintain completely filled d-subshells.

Only mercury lacks an incompletely filled d-subshell in all common oxidation states, making it not a transition element.

58880.subject: Chemistry
58880.text: Which from following solids is isotropic?
58880.sol:
The property of exhibiting identical physical properties in all directions is called isotropy.

Amorphous solids are isotropic due to their random particle arrangement, creating uniform average environments in all directions. Crystalline solids exhibit anisotropy because their ordered, repeating structures produce direction-dependent physical properties.

Among the options:
Glass is amorphous and isotropic.
Ceramics are typically crystalline and anisotropic.
Graphite's layered crystalline structure makes it anisotropic.
Ice's crystalline nature makes it anisotropic.

59196.subject: Chemistry
59196.text: Which from following ionic solids exhibits decrease in its solubility in water with increase of temperature?
59196.sol:
Among the given options, sodium sulfate $\left(\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4\right)$ exhibits a decrease in solubility with an increase in temperature. This behavior is unusual because, for most ionic solids, solubility tends to increase with temperature. However, for $\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{SO}_4$, its dissolution is exothermic, meaning it releases heat when it dissolves in water. According to Le Chatelier's principle, if the dissolution process is exothermic, increasing the temperature will shift the equilibrium to favor the undissolved solid, thereby reducing solubility at higher temperatures.
Solubility trends for other salts:
- (1) NaCl (Sodium chloride): NaCl 's solubility increases with temperature.
- (2) $\mathrm{KNO}_3$ (Potassium nitrate): $\mathrm{KNO}_3$ 's solubility increases significantly with temperature.
- (3) $\mathrm{NaNO}_3$ (Sodium nitrate): $\mathrm{NaNO}_3$ 's solubility also increases with temperature.

60259.text: The point on the curve $4 y^2-4 y+2 x-1=0$ at which the tangent becomes parallel toY-axis is
60259.sol:
The condition for a tangent to be parallel to the Y-axis is that $\frac{dx}{dy} = 0$.
Differentiate $4y^2 - 4y + 2x - 1 = 0$ with respect to $y$:

$8y - 4 + 2\frac{dx}{dy} = 0$

Solving for $\frac{dx}{dy}$ gives $\frac{dx}{dy} = 2 - 4y$.

Set $\frac{dx}{dy} = 0$, so $2 - 4y = 0$, yielding $y = \frac{1}{2}$.

Substitute into the original equation:

$4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2 - 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + 2x - 1 = 0$

$1 - 2 + 2x - 1 = 0$

$2x - 2 = 0$, so $x = 1$.

The point is $\left(1, \frac{1}{2}\right)$, corresponding to option A.

60738.subject: Mathematics
60738.text: The equation of the circle passing through the point $(1,1)$ and having two diameters along the pair of lines $x^2-y^2-2 x+4 y-3=0$ is
60738.sol:
The equation $x^2 - y^2 - 2x + 4y - 3 = 0$ represents a pair of intersecting lines, which are diameters of the circle. Since $B^2 - 4AC = 0 - 4(1)(-1) = 4 > 0$ and the condition for a pair of straight lines is satisfied, we factor it into two linear equations.

Assume the lines take the form $(x - y + c_1)(x + y + c_2) = 0$. Expanding gives $x^2 - y^2 + (c_1 + c_2)x + (c_1 - c_2)y + c_1c_2 = 0$.

Matching coefficients with the original equation yields:

$c_1 + c_2 = -2$

$c_1 - c_2 = 4$

$c_1c_2 = -3$

Adding the first two equations gives $2c_1 = 2$ so $c_1 = 1$, and substitution shows $c_2 = -3$, consistent with the third equation.

The diameters are thus $x - y + 1 = 0$ and $x + y - 3 = 0$.

Their intersection, the circle's center, is found by solving the system: adding the equations gives $2x - 2 = 0$ so $x = 1$, and substitution into $x + y - 3 = 0$ yields $y = 2$, giving center $(1,2)$.

The circle passes through $(1,1)$, so the radius squared is $r^2 = (1 - 1)^2 + (1 - 2)^2 = 1$.

The equation of the circle is $(x - 1)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 1$, which corresponds to option C.

61639.subject: Mathematics
61639.text: If $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x}\right)$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
61639.sol:
Given $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x}\right)$

We can simplify the expression inside the inverse trigonometric function using half-angle formulas:

$\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{\left(\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^2}{\cos^2 \dfrac{5x}{2} - \sin^2 \dfrac{5x}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}}{\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos \dfrac{5x}{2}$:

$\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{1 + \tan \dfrac{5x}{2}}{1 - \tan \dfrac{5x}{2}} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)$

Using the complementary angle identity $\tan \theta = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)$

Substituting this back into the original equation:

$y = \cot^{-1}\left[\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)\right]$

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{5}{2}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{5}{2}$

62518.subject: Mathematics
62518.sol:
Let $E = 2\sin^{-1}x + 3\cos^{-1}x$

Given $2\sin^{-1}x - 3\cos^{-1}x = 4$

Adding the two equations, we get:

$4\sin^{-1}x = E + 4 \Rightarrow \sin^{-1}x = \dfrac{E + 4}{4}$

Subtracting the second equation from the first, we get:

$6\cos^{-1}x = E - 4 \Rightarrow \cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{E - 4}{6}$

Using the identity $\sin^{-1}x + \cos^{-1}x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:

$\dfrac{E + 4}{4} + \dfrac{E - 4}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\dfrac{3(E + 4) + 2(E - 4)}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$\dfrac{5E + 4}{12} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$5E + 4 = 6\pi$

$E = \dfrac{6\pi - 4}{5}$

Answer: $\dfrac{6\pi - 4}{5}$

62544.subject: Mathematics
62544.sol:
The given expression is $\dfrac{\tan^{-1}(1) + \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)}{\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) - \sec^{-1}(-2)}$

Evaluating the terms in the numerator:
$\tan^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$
Using the identity $\sin^{-1}(x) + \cos^{-1}(x) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, we have $\cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$
Numerator $= \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4}$

Evaluating the terms in the denominator:
$\tan^{-1}(\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$
$\sec^{-1}(-2) = \pi - \sec^{-1}(2) = \pi - \dfrac{\pi}{3} = \dfrac{2\pi}{3}$
Denominator $= \dfrac{\pi}{3} - \dfrac{2\pi}{3} = -\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

Substituting these values back into the expression:
$\dfrac{\dfrac{3\pi}{4}}{-\dfrac{\pi}{3}} = \dfrac{3\pi}{4} \times \left(-\dfrac{3}{\pi}\right) = -\dfrac{9}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{-9}{4}$

62551.subject: Mathematics
62551.text: The minimum value of $(\sin^{-1} x)^2 + (\cos^{-1} x)^2$ is............
62551.sol:
Let $y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + (\cos^{-1} x)^2$

Using the identity $\sin^{-1} x + \cos^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$, we can write $\cos^{-1} x = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} x$

Substituting this into the expression for $y$:

$y = (\sin^{-1} x)^2 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1} x\right)^2$

Let $t = \sin^{-1} x$, where $t \in \left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

$y = t^2 + \left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - t\right)^2$

$y = 2t^2 - \pi t + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t^2 - \dfrac{\pi}{2}t\right) + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 - 2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{4}$

$y = 2\left(t - \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)^2 + \dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

The minimum value occurs when $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, which lies in the interval $\left[-\dfrac{\pi}{2}, \dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$

Therefore, the minimum value is $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi^2}{8}$

62971.text:
Which of the following statements has the truth value T ?
A: cube roots of unity are in Geometric progression and their sum is 1
B: $4+7 > 10$ iff $2+8 < 10$
C: $\exists x \in \mathbb{N}$ such that $x^2-3 x+2=0$ and $\exists \mathrm{n} \in \mathbb{N}$ such that n is an odd number
D : $3+\mathrm{i}$ is a complex number or $\sqrt{2}+\sqrt{3}=\sqrt{5}$
62971.sol:
Statement A: The cube roots of unity are $1$, $\omega$, and $\omega^2$ with $\omega = e^{i\cdot2\pi/3}$, which form a geometric progression with common ratio $\omega$. However, their sum is $1 + \omega + \omega^2 = 0 eq 1$. Thus, the conjunction is false.

Statement B: Since $4 + 7 = 11 > 10$ is true and $2 + 8 = 10 ot< 10$ is false, the biconditional is false.

Statement C: Solving $x^2 - 3x + 2 = 0$ yields $x = 1, 2 \in \mathbb{N}$, so there exists $x$ satisfying the equation. Natural numbers include odd integers, such as $1$. Thus, both components are true, and the conjunction is true.

Statement D: The expression $3 + i$ is a complex number, and while $\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3} = \sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3} eq \sqrt{5}, the disjunction is true because the first component is true.

Statements C and D are true, corresponding to option D.

$

The probability distribution of a random variable X is given by
$X = x$$1$$2$$3$$4$

63578.sol:

$k + 2k + 3k + 4k = 1$

$P(X=3) = \dfrac{3}{10}$
$P(X=4) = \dfrac{4}{10}$

The cumulative distribution function (c.d.f.) $F(x)$ is given by $F(x) = P(X \le x)$.

$F(1) = P(X \le 1) = P(X=1) = \dfrac{1}{10}$

$F(2) = P(X \le 2) = P(X=1) + P(X=2) = \dfrac{1}{10} + \dfrac{2}{10} = \dfrac{3}{10}$

$F(3) = P(X \le 3) = F(2) + P(X=3) = \dfrac{3}{10} + \dfrac{3}{10} = \dfrac{6}{10}$

$F(4) = P(X \le 4) = F(3) + P(X=4) = \dfrac{6}{10} + \dfrac{4}{10} = 1$

Answer:
$X = x$$1$$2$$3$$4$
$F(X = x)$$\dfrac{1}{10}$$\dfrac{3}{10}$$\dfrac{6}{10}$$1$

$(3)(5) + (-2)(b) + (7)(3) = 0$

$15 - 2b + 21 = 0$

$36 - 2b = 0$

$b = 18$

Answer: $b = 18$

65542.text: An alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin 100t$ volt is applied to a capacitor of capacity $2\ \mu\text{F}$. The root mean square value of current in the circuit is
65542.sol:
Given alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin(100t)$ V.

Comparing with the standard equation $e = E_0\sin(\omega t)$, we get:

Peak voltage $E_0 = 150\sqrt{2}$ V

Angular frequency $\omega = 100$ rad/s

The root mean square voltage is:

$E_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{150\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 150$ V

The capacitive reactance is:

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} = 5000\ \Omega$

The root mean square current in the circuit is:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_{\text{rms}}}{X_C} = \dfrac{150}{5000} = 0.03$ A

$I_{\text{rms}} = 30$ mA

Answer: $30$ mA

66771.subject: Physics
66771.text: Two concentric circular coils having radii $r_1$ and $r_2$ (r_2 < < r_1$) are placed co-axially with centres coinciding. The mutual inductance of the arrangement is (Both coils have single turn, \mu_0$ = permeability of free space)
66771.sol:
Let a current $I$ flow through the outer coil of radius $r_1$.

The magnetic field at the centre of the outer coil is given by $B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r_1}$.

Since $r_2 < < r_1$, this magnetic field can be considered uniform over the entire area of the inner coil.

The magnetic flux linked with the inner coil of radius $r_2$ is $\Phi = B \times A = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2r_1}\right) \times (\pi r_2^2)$.

The mutual inductance $M$ of the arrangement is defined as $M = \dfrac{\Phi}{I}$.

Substituting the value of $\Phi$, we get $M = \dfrac{\mu_0 \pi r_2^2}{2r_1}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\mu_0 r_2^2 \pi}{2r_1}$

66774.subject: Physics
66774.text: A coil of 'n' turns and resistance $R\,\Omega$ is connected in series with a resistance $R/4$. The combination is moved for time 't' second through flux $\Phi_1$ to $\Phi_2$. The induced current in the circuit is
66774.sol:
The total resistance of the circuit is given by the sum of the coil's resistance and the series resistance:

$R_{eq} = R + \dfrac{R}{4} = \dfrac{5R}{4}$

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the average induced emf in a coil of $n$ turns is:

$E = -n \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = -n \dfrac{\Phi_2 - \Phi_1}{t} = \dfrac{n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t}$

The induced current in the circuit is the ratio of the induced emf to the total resistance:

$I = \dfrac{E}{R_{eq}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{t}}{\dfrac{5R}{4}} = \dfrac{4n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{5Rt}$

Using $T$ for time as given in the options, the induced current is $\dfrac{4n(\Phi_1 - \Phi_2)}{5RT}$.

66801.text: When a current in the conducting coil is changed from 5 A in one direction to 5 A in opposite direction in 0.5 second, an average induced e.m.f in the coil is 2 V. The self-inductance of the coil is
66801.sol:
The induced eMF in a coil due to self-inductance follows $E = -L \frac{dI}{dt}$, where $L$ represents the self-inductance and $\frac{dI}{dt}$ the rate of current change. Given the initial current $I_1 = 5$ A and final current $I_2 = -5$ A, the current change is $\Delta I = -10$ A over $\Delta t = 0.5$ s, with an average induced eMF magnitude of $2$ V.

The magnitude equation simplifies to $E_{\text{avg}} = L \left| \frac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \right|$. Substituting values gives $2 = L \left| \frac{-10}{0.5} \right| = L \times 20$, leading to $L = \frac{2}{20} = 0.1$ H.

Converting to millihenrys yields $L = 0.1 \times 1000 = 100$ mH.

The self-inductance is 100 mH, corresponding to option D.

Considering force balance in the orbit:

Gravitational force balances the centrifugal force. The orbital speed can be obtained as:

68007.text: A wire has mass $(0.3 \pm 0.003)$ gram, radius $(0.5 \pm 0.005)$ mm and length $(6 \pm 0.06)$ cm. The maximum error in the measurement of density is
68007.sol:
Density of the wire is given by $\rho = \dfrac{m}{\pi r^2 l}$

The maximum percentage error in density is

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = \left( \dfrac{\Delta m}{m} + 2 \dfrac{\Delta r}{r} + \dfrac{\Delta l}{l} \right) \times 100$

Given values are:

$\dfrac{\Delta m}{m} \times 100 = \dfrac{0.003}{0.3} \times 100 = 1\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta r}{r} \times 100 = \dfrac{0.005}{0.5} \times 100 = 1\%$

$\dfrac{\Delta l}{l} \times 100 = \dfrac{0.06}{6} \times 100 = 1\%$

Substituting these values, we get:

$\dfrac{\Delta \rho}{\rho} \times 100 = 1\% + 2(1\%) + 1\% = 4\%$

Answer: $4\%$

68666.text:
Two simple pendulums of lengths $L_1$ and $L_2$ have periodic time $T_1$ and $T_2$ respectively $(T_1 > T_2)$. The time period of the pendulum of length $(L_1-L_2)$ is
$[(L_1-L_2) > 60\text{ cm}]$
68666.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum of length $L$ is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L}{g}}$.

Squaring both sides gives $T^2 = \dfrac{4\pi^2 L}{g}$, which implies $L = \dfrac{g T^2}{4\pi^2}$.

For the first pendulum, $L_1 = \dfrac{g T_1^2}{4\pi^2}$.

For the second pendulum, $L_2 = \dfrac{g T_2^2}{4\pi^2}$.

The length of the new pendulum is $L' = L_1 - L_2$.

Substituting the values of $L_1$ and $L_2$ gives $L' = \dfrac{g}{4\pi^2} (T_1^2 - T_2^2)$.

The time period $T'$ of the new pendulum is $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{L'}{g}}$.

Substituting $L'$ gives $T' = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{g(T_1^2 - T_2^2)}{4\pi^2 g}} = \sqrt{T_1^2 - T_2^2}$.

Answer: $\sqrt{T_1^2 - T_2^2}$

69943.subject: Physics
69943.text: In the thermodynamic processes, which of the following statements is <u>NOT</u> true?
options: In an isothermal process, the temperature remains constant.
In an adiabatic process, the system is insulated from surroundings.
In an isochoric process, pressure remains constant.
69943.sol:
The analysis focuses on identifying the false statement among thermodynamic process definitions.

Isothermal processes maintain constant temperature ($T = \text{constant}$), confirming truth for option A.

Adiabatic processes involve no heat exchange ($Q = 0$), validating option B.

Isochoric processes are defined by constant volume ($V = \text{constant}$), whereas constant pressure defines isobaric processes ($P = \text{constant}$). Option C incorrectly conflates these, making it false.

For adiabatic processes involving ideal gases, $PV^{\gamma} = \text{constant}$ holds true, supporting option D.

The false statement is option C.

70659.text: On closing an open organ pipe from one end, it is noticed that the frequency of third harmonic is $50 \mathrm{ Hz}$ more than the fundamental frequency of vibration in open organ pipe. The fundamental frequency of open organ pipe is
70659.sol:
Frequency of $\mathrm{m}^{\text{th }}$ harmonic in an open organ pipe is $f_m=\frac{m v}{2 L}$
Fundamental frequency in an open organ pipe, for $m=1 f_1=\frac{v}{2 L}$
Frequency of nth harmonic in a closed organ pipe, $f_n^{\prime}=\frac{n v}{4 L}$
Frequency of 3rd harmonic in a closed organ pipe, $f^{\prime}{ }_3=\frac{3 v}{4 L}$
Now, $f_3^{\prime}-f_1=50\frac{3 v}{4 L}-\frac{v}{2 L}=50 \Rightarrow \frac{v}{L}=200$
Thus, fundamental frequency in an open organ pipe,
$f_1=\frac{v}{2 L}=\frac{200}{2} \mathrm{ Hz}=100 $$\mathrm{ Hz}$

71287.subject: Biology
71287.text: A promoter in a transcription unit is a DNA sequence ________.
options: that provides a binding site for RNA polymerase
that provides the binding site for DNA polymerase
71287.sol:
A promoter is a specific DNA sequence in a transcription unit that provides a binding site for RNA polymerase and transcription factors to initiate the process of transcription.

It is located towards the $5'$ end (upstream) of the structural gene with respect to the coding strand.

The promoter itself is not transcribed into RNA, nor does it terminate transcription (which is the function of the terminator sequence). DNA polymerase binds to origins of replication during DNA replication, not to promoters during transcription.

Answer: that provides a binding site for RNA polymerase

71515.subject: Biology
71515.text:
Arrange the following events of microsporogenesis in the correct sequence:
A) Meiosis
B) Sporogenous tissue
C) Microspore mother cell
D) Microspore tetrads
E) Pollen grain
71515.sol:
In a young anther, a group of compactly arranged homogenous cells called the sporogenous tissue occupies the centre of each microsporangium.

As the anther develops, the cells of the sporogenous tissue differentiate to function as microspore mother cells (MMCs).

Each microspore mother cell undergoes meiosis.

The meiotic division results in the formation of a cluster of four haploid cells called the microspore tetrad.

As the anthers mature and dehydrate, the microspores dissociate from each other and develop into pollen grains.

The correct sequence of events is Sporogenous tissue \rightarrow Microspore mother cell \rightarrow Meiosis \rightarrow Microspore tetrads \rightarrow Pollen grain, which corresponds to $B \rightarrow C \rightarrow A \rightarrow D \rightarrow E$.

Answer: $B \rightarrow C \rightarrow A \rightarrow D \rightarrow E$

71937.subject: Chemistry
71937.text: A metal forms fcc unit cell with unit edge length $400\ \text{pm}$. Calculate the number of atoms present in $0.6\ \text{g}$ of metal if the density of metal is $12.0\ \text{g/cm}^3$
71937.sol:
Edge length of the unit cell, $a = 400\ \text{pm} = 4 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm}$

Volume of the unit cell, $V = a^3 = (4 \times 10^{-8}\ \text{cm})^3 = 64 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{cm}^3$

Mass of one unit cell = Volume $\times$ Density = $64 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{cm}^3 \times 12.0\ \text{g/cm}^3 = 768 \times 10^{-24}\ \text{g}$

Number of unit cells in $0.6\ \text{g}$ of metal = $\dfrac{0.6}{768 \times 10^{-24}} = \dfrac{600}{768} \times 10^{21} = 0.78125 \times 10^{21}$

Since the metal forms an fcc unit cell, the number of atoms per unit cell is $4$.

Total number of atoms = $4 \times 0.78125 \times 10^{21} = 3.125 \times 10^{21}$

Answer: $3.125 \times 10^{21}$

72044.subject: Chemistry
72044.text: Which of the following processes is an example of decrease in entropy?
options: Dissolution of solid iodine in water
Formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas
Dissociation of hydrogen molecules into atoms
Decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating
72044.sol:
Entropy is a measure of the randomness or disorder of a system. A decrease in entropy occurs when the randomness of the system decreases, which typically happens when the number of gaseous moles decreases or when a substance changes from a more disordered state (gas) to a less disordered state (liquid or solid).

For the dissolution of solid iodine in water: $I_{2}(s) \rightarrow I_{2}(aq)$. The solid lattice breaks down and molecules disperse in the solvent, leading to an increase in entropy (\Delta S > 0$).

For the formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas: 2H_{2}(g) + O_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2H_{2}O(l)$. Here, $3$ moles of gaseous reactants form $2$ moles of liquid product. The number of gaseous moles decreases (\Delta n_{g} = -3$), and the system goes from a highly disordered gaseous state to a more ordered liquid state. Thus, entropy decreases (\Delta S < 0$).

For the dissociation of hydrogen molecules into atoms: $H_{2}(g) \rightarrow 2H(g)$. One mole of gas forms two moles of gas. The number of particles increases, leading to an increase in entropy (\Delta S > 0$).

For the decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating: $CaCO_{3}(s) \rightarrow CaO(s) + CO_{2}(g)$. A solid decomposes to form a solid and a gas. The production of gas increases the randomness, leading to an increase in entropy (\Delta S > 0$).

Therefore, the formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas is the only process that results in a decrease in entropy.

Answer: Formation of liquid water from hydrogen and oxygen gas

72190.subject: Physics
72190.text: The north pole of the magnet is brought near a metallic ring as shown in figure. The direction of induced current in the ring (if looked from upside) will be
72190.sol:
As the north pole of the magnet is brought near the metallic ring, the downward magnetic flux linked with the ring increases.

According to Lenz's law, the induced current in the ring will flow in a direction such that it opposes the change in magnetic flux. To oppose the increasing downward flux, the induced current must produce an upward magnetic field.

Using the right-hand grip rule, an upward magnetic field is generated when the current flows in an anti-clockwise direction. Therefore, when viewed from above, the direction of the induced current in the ring will be anti-clockwise.

Answer: anti-clockwise.

Therefore, the correct relationship between the wavelengths is:
$\lambda_1 < \lambda_3 < \lambda_2$

Answer: $\lambda_1 < \lambda_3 < \lambda_2$

73775.subject: General Ability
73775.text: A ball is dropped from rest from height $h$ above the ground in frame $S$ (the Earth's frame). Another frame $S'$ is moving upwards with constant speed $u$ relative to the Earth. In frame $S'$, the ball has initial downward speed $v$. Pertaining to the change in kinetic energy $(\Delta K)$ of the ball from release to just before hitting the ground as measured in frames $S$ and $S'$ separately, which one of the following is correct?
options: $\Delta K$ is the same in both the frames.
$\Delta K$ cannot be compared without the information of mass of the ball.
73775.sol:
In frame $S$ (Earth's frame):

Initial velocity of the ball, $v_{i} = 0$

Final velocity of the ball just before hitting the ground, $v_{f} = \sqrt{2gh}$ (downwards)

Change in kinetic energy in frame $S$ is:

$\Delta K_{S} = \dfrac{1}{2} m v_{f}^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} m v_{i}^2 = \dfrac{1}{2} m (2gh) - 0 = mgh$

In frame $S'$ (moving upwards with constant speed $u$):

Initial velocity of the ball, $v'_{i} = u = v$ (downwards)

Final velocity of the ball, $v'_{f} = \sqrt{2gh} + v$ (downwards)

Change in kinetic energy in frame $S'$ is:

$\Delta K_{S'} = \dfrac{1}{2} m (v'_{f})^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} m (v'_{i})^2$

$\Delta K_{S'} = \dfrac{1}{2} m (\sqrt{2gh} + v)^2 - \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$

$\Delta K_{S'} = \dfrac{1}{2} m (2gh + v^2 + 2v\sqrt{2gh}) - \dfrac{1}{2} m v^2$

$\Delta K_{S'} = mgh + mv\sqrt{2gh}$

Comparing the two expressions, we get $\Delta K_{S'} = \Delta K_{S} + mv\sqrt{2gh}$.

Since $m, v, g, h$ are all positive quantities, $\Delta K_{S'} > \Delta K_{S}$.

Therefore, the change in kinetic energy is larger in frame $S'$.

Answer: $\Delta K$ is larger in frame $S'$.

77280.subject: Mathematics
77280.text:
Passage: The foci of the ellipse $px^2+16y^2=16p$ and the foci of the hyperbola $25(81x^2-144y^2)=11664$ coincide (assume $p< 16$).

Question: What is the difference between the eccentricities of the hyperbola and the ellipse ?
77280.sol:
The equation of the ellipse can be written as $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{p} = 1$.

Since $p < 16$, the major axis is along the x-axis. The eccentricity $e_1$ of the ellipse is given by $e_1 = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{p}{16}}$.

The foci of the ellipse are $(\pm 4e_1, 0) = \left(\pm 4\sqrt{1 - \dfrac{p}{16}}, 0\right) = (\pm \sqrt{16 - p}, 0)$.

The equation of the hyperbola is $25(81x^2 - 144y^2) = 11664$.

Dividing by $11664$, we get $\dfrac{25x^2}{144} - \dfrac{25y^2}{81} = 1 \Rightarrow \dfrac{x^2}{144/25} - \dfrac{y^2}{81/25} = 1$.

The eccentricity $e_2$ of the hyperbola is $e_2 = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{81/25}{144/25}} = \sqrt{1 + \dfrac{81}{144}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{225}{144}} = \dfrac{15}{12} = \dfrac{5}{4} = 1.25$.

The foci of the hyperbola are $(\pm A e_2, 0) = \left(\pm \dfrac{12}{5} \times \dfrac{5}{4}, 0\right) = (\pm 3, 0)$.

Since the foci of the ellipse and the hyperbola coincide, we have $\sqrt{16 - p} = 3 \Rightarrow 16 - p = 9 \Rightarrow p = 7$.

The eccentricity of the ellipse is $e_1 = \sqrt{1 - \dfrac{7}{16}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{9}{16}} = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$.

The difference between the eccentricities is $e_2 - e_1 = 1.25 - 0.75 = 0.5$.

Answer: $0\cdot5$

79488.subject: Botany
79488.text:
Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata?

(a) In Urochordata, notochord extends from head to tail, and it is present throughout their life.

(b) In Vertebrata, the notochord is present during the embryonic period only.

(c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.

(d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla: Hemichordata, Tunicata, and Cephalochordata.
79488.sol:
Fundamental characters of phylum chordates:
1. Presence of notochord: They are characterized by the presence of rod-like supporting notochord extending throughout the length of the body.
2. Presence of dorsal tubular nerve cord: They are characterized by the presence of dorsal nerve cord lying above the notochord.
3. Presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits: They are characterized by the presence of paired pharyngeal gill slits at some stage of their lifetime.
4. Presences of ventral heart: They are characterized by a ventral heart, i.e. heart is situated on the ventral side of the alimentary canal in the body cavity.
5. Presence of post-anal tail.
6. Body cavity: They are coelomates, Triploblsatic body, and bilaterally symmetrical animals.

Phylum Chordata is divided into three sub-phyla:
1. Urochordata (Gr: aura-tail): Here, the notochord is confined only to the tall region of the larva. It is represented by primitive chordates like Ascidia, Herdmania, commonly called ‘sea squirt’.
2. Cephalochordate (Gr: cephalon-head): Here, the notochord is well-developed, extending from the anterior to the posterior region of the body. Anteriorly, it extends beyond the nerve cord. Hence, the name cephalochordate. It includes primitive chordates like Amphioxus. Since the above two subphyla include primitive chordates, they are also called Protochordata.
3. Vertebrata or Craniata: Here, the notochord is replaced by the vertebral column.

C. Extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell form mesosomes.
D. Tails towards the inner part of lipids are hydrophobic and thus protected from aqueous medium.
E. Glycocalyx is present on the outer surface of the plasma membrane.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
79695.sol:
Statement A is correct. Chemical studies on human red blood cells (RBCs) show that the cell membrane consists of approximately $52\%$ protein and $40\%$ lipids.

Statement B is correct. The cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids, primarily phospholipids, which are arranged in a bilayer.

Statement C is incorrect. Mesosomes are formed by the extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell in prokaryotes, not in eukaryotic cells.

Statement D is correct. The lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar hydrophilic heads towards the outer sides and the non-polar hydrophobic tails towards the inner part, ensuring that the non-polar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.

Since statement C is incorrect for eukaryotic cells, any option containing C is eliminated. Thus, statements A, B, and D are the correct choices.

Answer: A, B and D only

It supports the hypothesis that IAA is auxin.
It demonstrated polar movements of auxins
80259.sol:
Darwin and his son observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source. This is called phototropism. They performed series of experiments which concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile. F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings and concluded that phototropism of oat seedlings occur. They also concluded that phototropism in the tips of coleoptiles is due to the polar movement of auxin in the stem.
So, the correct answer is 'it demonstrated polar movements of auxins'.

81748.subject: Chemistry
81748.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I : Heating NaCl with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ and MnO$_2$ results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement-II : Heating NaI with concentrated H$_2$SO$_4$ and MnO$_2$ results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
81748.sol:
The reaction of $\text{NaCl}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ is given by:

$2\text{NaCl} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{Cl}_2$

In this reaction, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ changes from $+4$ in $\text{MnO}_2$ to $+2$ in $\text{MnSO}_4$. Since the oxidation state decreases, $\text{Mn}$ undergoes reduction, not oxidation. Thus, Statement-I is incorrect.

The reaction of $\text{NaI}$ with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ and $\text{MnO}_2$ is given by:

$2\text{NaI} + \text{MnO}_2 + 2\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 + \text{MnSO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{I}_2$

Here, the oxidation state of $\text{Mn}$ also changes from $+4$ to $+2$, which means $\text{Mn}$ undergoes reduction. Thus, Statement-II is correct.

Therefore, Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

Answer: Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

85870.subject: Biology
85870.text: In a haplodiploid ant species, sons are haploid and produced from unfertilized eggs, while daughters are diploid and produced from fertilized eggs. A single queen establishes a colony after mating with three different unrelated males. The queen uses the sperm from all three males equally to produce her female offspring. The average genetic relatedness between two randomly selected female offspring in this colony will be:
85870.sol:
In a haplodiploid system, females are diploid, receiving half of their genes from the mother (queen) and half from the father (male). Males are haploid, meaning all sperm produced by a single male are genetically identical.

The genetic relatedness between two full sisters (sharing the same father) is $0.75$. This is because they share $100\%$ of their paternal genes ($0.5 \times 1 = 0.5$) and $50\%$ of their maternal genes ($0.5 \times 0.5 = 0.25$), giving $0.5 + 0.25 = 0.75$.

The genetic relatedness between two half-sisters (having different fathers) is $0.25$. They share $0\%$ of their paternal genes (since the males are unrelated) and $50\%$ of their maternal genes, giving $0 + 0.25 = 0.25$.

Since the queen mates with $3$ males and uses their sperm equally, the probability that two randomly selected daughters share the same father is $\dfrac{1}{3}$, and the probability that they have different fathers is $\dfrac{2}{3}$.

The average genetic relatedness ($r_{avg}$) is the weighted average of these probabilities:

$r_{avg} = $\$left(\dfrac{1}{3} \times0.75\right) + \$ left($\dfrac{2}{3} \times 0.25\right)$

$r_{avg} = 0.25 + \dfrac{0.50}{3}$

$r_{avg} = 0.25 + 0.1667 = 0.4167$

Rounding to three decimal places, the average genetic relatedness is $0.417$.

Answer: $0.417$

90123.sol:
Let, the point $\left(0, a\right)$ lie inside the circle whose end-points of the diameter are $\left(- 2,0\right)$ and $\left(1,1\right)$, but does not lie on this diameter
$⇒ \left(0, a\right)$ lie inside the circle $\left(x + 2\right)\left(x - 1\right) + y\left(y - 1\right) = 0$
$⇒ \left(0 + 2\right)\left(0 - 1\right) + a\left(a - 1\right) < 0$
$⇒ {a}^{2} - a - 2 < 0 ⇒ \left(a - 2\right)\left(a + 1\right) < 0$
$⇒ a \in \left(- 1, 2\right)$
But, $a \ne \dfrac{2}{3}$ because at $a = \dfrac{2}{3}$, points $\left(0, \dfrac{2}{3}\right), \left(- 2, 0\right)$ and $\left(1, 1\right)$ are collinear
$⇒ a \in \left(- 1, 2\right) - \left\{\dfrac{2}{3}\right\}$ 

Hence, the sum of all possible integral values of $‘a’$ is $1$

93309.text: Two particles of masses $m$ and $2m$ are kept at a distance $a.$ Find the speed of particles and their relative velocity of approach when separation becomes $a / 2.$
93309.sol:
In arrangements $\left(1\right)$ and $\left(2\right),$

Momentum conservation,

$0 = m{v}_{1} - 2m{v}_{2}$ ...(i)

Energy conservation

$- \dfrac{Gm ⋅ 2m}{a} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{v}_{1}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}2m{v}_{2}^{2} - \dfrac{Gm ⋅ 2m}{a / 2}$ ...(ii)

From Equation (i), we get

${v}_{1} = 2{v}_{2}$

Putting this value $\left({v}_{1} = 2{v}_{2}\right)$ in Equation (ii), we get

$- \dfrac{2Gm^{2}}{a} = \dfrac{1}{2}m{\left(2{v}_{2}\right)}^{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}2m{v}_{2}^{2} - \dfrac{4Gm^{2}}{a}$

$3m{v}_{2}^{2} = \dfrac{2Gm^{2}}{a}$

${v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{3a}}$

Relative velocity ${v}_{1, 2} = {v}_{1} + {v}_{2}$

$= 3\sqrt{\dfrac{2Gm}{3a}}$

$= \sqrt{\dfrac{6Gm}{a}}$

Radially symmetrical: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry and the organisms possessing it are& called radially symmetric. For e.g.,& some sponges, coelenterates, ctenophores, adult echinoderms.

96082.text: All of the following processes occur in the endomembrane system, except
96082.sol:
The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system.

Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins.&

The smooth endoplasmic reticulum is the major site for synthesis of lipid. In animal cells lipid-like steroidal hormones are synthesised in SER.

Protein synthesis and its modification process are carried out by the organelles of endoplasmic system.& Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids.

In Amoeba, the contractile vacuole is important for excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.
